# typed-sql 2.5.0

typed-sql 2.5 adds SQL Server and DuckDB grammars, native nested-value execution,
and SQL-file parameter and application identity support. The stable package train is published as
`2.5.0` on npm's `latest` tag after qualification of `2.5.0-rc.0` on `next`.
The preview-backed packages retain their experimental prerelease versions.

## Highlights

- `@typed-sql/sqlserver` owns T-SQL syntax, catalog evidence, coercion and nullability
  rules, native type policies, verification, and plan capture. Its application-owned
  direct ODBC adapter qualifies boxed SQL Server 2017–2025 across ten engine and
  compatibility-level combinations on Linux x64. The explicit `msnodesqlv8`
  compatibility adapter has additional text-result restrictions.
- `@typed-sql/duckdb` supports analytical SQL and typed LIST, ARRAY, STRUCT, TUPLE,
  MAP, and UNION values. Its optional Node SDK adapter includes native vector appends,
  transactions, cancellation, verification, and plan capture. Exact qualified pairs
  are DuckDB 1.5.6 with `@duckdb/node-api` 1.5.6-r.2 and DuckDB 2.0.0 with SDK 2.0.0-r.1.
- SQL files support named argument objects and repeated or reordered numbered
  bindings. Imported SQL assets participate in manifests, live verification, plan
  capture, and migration compatibility reports.
- `withSchemaBrands`, `Brand`, and `brandValue` preserve explicit application
  identities through projections and column-context parameters without changing
  primitive database transport.
- Native value plans preserve independently nullable nested objects, tuples,
  fixed-length arrays, typed NULLs, and empty collections. Live verification can
  compare physical database types when their JavaScript types are identical.
- The SQLite Wasm OO1 adapter preserves lossless INTEGER values and application
  ownership of the driver and storage VFS. SQLite qualification includes 3.54.1.
- The playground and packaged language-server checks cover all five grammars.

Unsupported, ambiguous, and dynamic SQL continues to fail closed. Grammar packages
remain independent of database drivers; applications install drivers for the
explicit execution or introspection adapters they use.

## Compatibility

The runtime requires Node.js 22.11 or newer. The project-wide correctness compiler
uses TypeScript 7.0.2. Individual adapters, native SDKs, and build hosts have their own
documented requirements. PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite are stable dialect packages;
SQL Server and DuckDB join the same stable package contract within their qualified
configurations. Their new integrations have less regression history than the older grammars.

See the [compatibility matrix](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/reference/compatibility),
[SQL Server guide](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/dialects/sqlserver),
[DuckDB guide](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/dialects/duckdb), and
[upgrade guide](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/guides/upgrading-from-v1).

## Package tracks

The stable package train contains `@typed-sql/core`, `@typed-sql/opentelemetry`,
`@typed-sql/ast`, `@typed-sql/schema`, `@typed-sql/config`, `@typed-sql/compiler`,
`@typed-sql/conformance`, `@typed-sql/postgres`, `@typed-sql/mysql`,
`@typed-sql/sqlite`, `@typed-sql/sqlserver`, `@typed-sql/duckdb`, `@typed-sql/cli`,
`@typed-sql/adapters`, and `@typed-sql/build`. Sharing a prerelease version does not
make the experimental packages stable or promote the release candidate to `latest`.

`@typed-sql/ts-bridge`, `@typed-sql/language-server`, and editor integrations remain experimental.
The pinned native TypeScript preview watcher can miss rapid edits on macOS during
directory subscription changes, including in ordinary TypeScript projects without
typed-sql. SQL declarations retain type dependencies across SQL errors to reduce
watch churn, but this does not resolve the upstream defect. Explicit compiler
checks remain the way to check current files when watch diagnostics are stale.
